chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man had two witnesses testify for him that he had fifty dirhams with a man, and two others came and testified that he had one hundred dirhams with him; all of them testified in one standing. He (peace be upon him) said: Cast lots among them, then make those upon whom the lot fell swear by Allah that they are swearing with the truth.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence handle conflicting witness testimonies for different debt amounts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the Shia legal mechanism for resolving contradictory witness testimonies through random selection (qar') followed by an oath (yamin), a method attributed to Imam al-Baqir (AS). It highlights the reliance on probabilistic justice in civil disputes when definitive evidence is lacking, ensuring the creditor receives a just determination based on the sworn testimony of the selected witnesses. This procedure underscores the practical application of divine guidance in daily commercial and legal affairs within the Shia jurisprudential tradition.
